topic: The Geometric Intuition of Cross Products and Linear Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The 2D Area Intuition
lecture_lines: Determinants represent the area of a parallelogram.
Scaling a vector scales the parallelogram area linearly.
Determinants track how space is scaled globally.
animations: Create a 2D coordinate system and display two vectors v1 and v2. #FFFFFF
Fill the parallelogram formed by v1 and v2 with a semi-transparent blue. #00FFFF
Label the area as 'Determinant' near the parallelogram. #FF00FF

sections.title: Defining the Cross Product via the Parallelogram
lecture_lines: Move to 3D with two distinct vectors.
The cross product produces a perpendicular vector.
Its magnitude is the parallelogram's surface area.
animations: Display vectors u and v originating from the same point. #FFFFFF
Draw the parallelogram using dashed lines to connect the vectors. #00FFFF
Create an arrow pointing perpendicular to the parallelogram to represent the cross product. #FFFF00

sections.title: The Linear Transformation Link: Determinants in 3D
lecture_lines: The scalar triple product computes volume.
Cross products relate to volumetric transformations.
It scales the volume of the unit cube.
Linear transformations squash or stretch space volume.
Cross products describe face normals in 3D.
animations: Show a unit cube aligned with the XYZ axes. #FFFFFF
Animate a linear transformation stretching the cube into a parallelepiped. #00FFFF
Display a volume label that updates dynamically during the transformation. #FFFF00
Highlight one face of the parallelepiped to show its orientation. #FF00FF
Fade out the transformation and show the final parallelepiped. #FFFFFF

sections.title: Geometric Application: The Normal Vector
lecture_lines: Surface normals are vital for 3D lighting.
Cross products compute these normals efficiently.
Light reflection depends on surface orientation.
Lighting calculations use normals for pixel color.
Physics simulations rely on these geometric tools.
animations: Render a flat triangle surface in 3D space using. #FFFFFF
Draw two vectors defining the sides of the triangle. #FFFF00
Use the cross product to generate the normal vector pointing outwards. #FF00FF
Rotate the triangle to show the normal vector remains perpendicular. #FF00FF
Show light rays bouncing off the surface using the normal vector and. #00FFFF

sections.title: Summary: The 'Flow' of Cross Products
lecture_lines: Magnitude is area, direction is normal.
Cross product bridges geometry and algebra.
It is central to modern 3D rendering.
